explanation: The base case only checks for the exact value `n === 0`. When `n` starts odd, subtracting 2 each call produces the sequence ...3, 1, -1, -3... which never lands exactly on 0. The recursion never hits its base case and keeps decrementing indefinitely, eventually causing a stack overflow — but only for odd starting values; even inputs terminate fine.
prompt: This countdown function works fine for some inputs but crashes for others. What's the bug?
choices: The base case only matches `n === 0`, so odd starting values skip past 0 and recurse forever without terminating
`console.log(n)` should be called after the recursive call instead of before it
The recursive step should use `n - 1` instead of `n - 2` for better performance
The function never returns a value from the recursive call, causing a silent failure
The recursive call should be `countDown(n)` instead of `countDown(n - 2)`
